title: Shedge and Nigam's 85-Run Stand Saves India A From Whitewash vs Australia A
excerpt: Suryansh Shedge's 66 and Vipraj Nigam's all-round show lifted India A from 159/6 to a 49-run win at Puducherry — Australia A took the series 2–1.
body:
• India A beat Australia A by 49 runs in the third unofficial ODI at Puducherry on October 11, avoiding a series whitewash — Australia A took the series 2–1.
  • Suryansh Shedge (66 off 60) and Vipraj Nigam (40 off 44) added 85 runs for the seventh wicket after India A had slumped to 159 for 6, lifting the hosts to 275.
  • Nigam then removed the dangerous Josh Philippe (56) lbw as Australia A folded for 226; Gurjapneet Singh took 3 for 56.
  • What this means for you: Shedge and Nigam — both proven IPL performers — have put their names firmly in the senior-team conversation ahead of a packed home season.

India A were staring at a whitewash at 159 for 6 in the 30th over. Ninety minutes later, they had 275 on the board and the beginnings of a famous escape. Suryansh Shedge's 66 off 60 balls and Vipraj Nigam's 40 off 44 — an 85-run seventh-wicket stand off 77 balls — dragged the hosts out of trouble at the Cricket Association Puducherry Siechem Ground, and India A went on to beat Australia A by 49 runs in the third unofficial ODI on October 11. Australia A took the series 2–1, but the whitewash was avoided in style.

The rescue act

The collapse had been swift. After a platform of 49 from Priyansh Arya and 39 from Prabhsimran Singh, India A lost five wickets for 71 runs — Ruturaj Gaikwad's 33 the only other contribution of note — as Ben Dwarshuis (3 for 38) and Will Sutherland (3 for 44) tore through the middle order. At 159 for 6, with the tail exposed, the innings was drifting toward the sub-200 totals that had defined the first two defeats.

"Australia A took the series 2–1, but the whitewash was avoided in style."

Shedge and Nigam had other plans. Shedge, striking at 110 with seven fours and two sixes, took the attack to Australia A's seamers; Nigam, all timing with six fours in his 44-ball 40, rotated and punished in equal measure. Their 85-run stand — the highest partnership of the match — pushed India A to 275 all out in 47.3 overs, with 24 extras padding a total that felt 60 runs above par at the innings break. Liam Scott (2 for 26) was the pick of the supporting cast.

Nigam strikes with the ball

Australia A's chase never truly got going. Josh Philippe's 56 off 48 threatened briefly, but Nigam — completing a genuine all-round performance — trapped him lbw for 1 for 47 from his ten overs, and the innings subsided to 226 all out in 46.2 overs. Gurjapneet Singh took 3 for 56, Yash Thakur 2 for 35 and Nishant Sindhu 2 for 42, while Anukul Roy's miserly 1 for 19 from six overs choked the middle overs. Nathan McSweeney (39), Lachlan Shaw (31) and Nikhil Chaudhary (29) all started without converting.

Series context

The win salvaged pride from a series Australia A had dominated: 125-run and 69-run victories in the first two unofficial ODIs on October 6 and 9, where India A were bowled out for 149 and 206 chasing 274 and 275. Full scorecard via CricketAddictor.

Why it matters

India A fixtures are auditions, and Shedge and Nigam just gave the selectors a tape worth rewinding. Both are proven IPL commodities — Shedge's power-hitting and Nigam's leg-spin-plus-lower-order-hitting are exactly the multi-skill profiles modern white-ball squads hoard. With a packed home season ahead and senior-team spots in flux, a match-winning all-round show against a strong Australia A attack is the loudest statement either could make.
